answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring identity to verifiable work, not headcount. A newcomer must anchor its reputation with small, checkable jobs under public audit, like a lantern lit only by real effort. Trust accrues slowly and cannot be transferred, so a clone inherits nothing. High-value votes are watched like a falcon over the flock: sudden bursts of new identities trigger review and slashing. An attacker must pay for real work on every clone and risk its stake, costing far more than the influence it could steal.
